headline: Voted not to recommend rezoning 430 and 432 Putnam Hill Road; recommended revised accessory apartment bylaw changes.
summary: Les Stevens presented a citizen's petition to rezone 430 and 432 Putnam Hill Road from R-1 to V. Residents raised concerns about wells, septic systems, and the character of the Village. The accessory apartment bylaw now mirrors state law and drops a waiver provision, and Town Meeting is scheduled for September 21, 2026.
decisions: Voted not to recommend that Town Meeting approve rezoning 430 and 432 Putnam Hill Road from R-1 to V, 5-0.
Recommended that Town Meeting approve the revised amendments to the accessory apartment bylaw, 5-0.

transcript:
# SUTTON PLANNING BOARD

**Meeting Minutes**

**August 17, 2026**

Approved

E. McCallum read the following notice: Pursuant to Governor Healey's directive extending the temporary Open Meeting provisions until June 30, 2027, the Planning Board meeting will be conducted in a HYBRID format and will be recorded. \*Recordings will be available on the Town's website and YouTube channel. \*Please be aware: Participants attending via Zoom will have their video and audio disabled. \*If you wish to engage in discussion, raise your hand; if acknowledged by the Chair, you will receive a pop-up message allowing you to unmute yourself. For agenda, YouTube, and Zoom links, please visit www.suttonma.org/cable-department.

Present in person: M. Gagan, W. Talcott, R. Largess Jr., W. Stanhope, E. McCallum, Dave Mason, Associate

Present remotely: none

Absent: none

Staff: J. Hager, Community Development Director

As the public hearing was not scheduled to start until 7:15 PM, the Board handled Action and Administrative Items:

## Action Items

ANR Plans – none

## Administrative Items

### Minutes

Motion: To approve the minutes of 8/3/26, R. Largess Jr.
2nd: E. McCallum
Vote: 4-0-1, E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Talcott – abstained as he wasn't present at this meeting, W. Stanhope - aye

Filings for August 31 – none – This meeting is cancelled.

Site Visit Report – none

Correspondence - none

Other Board Business - none

## Public Hearings

### Proposed Bylaw Changes

W. Talcott read the hearing Notice as it appeared in the Telegram & Gazette.

### Citizen's Petition – Rezoning R-1 to V 430 & 432 Putnam Hill Road

Les Stevens, resident of Douglas and co-owner of 430 Putnam Hill Road was present to discuss the citizen's petition. Mr. Stevens stated in the process of considering multifamily development on his lot and potential the adjacent land, town's people suggested perhaps he should re-zone the entire parcels to allow for more entry level housing. He noted zoning east of Putnam Hill Road is 500' deep but only 200' feet deep west of Putnam Hill. He stated the re-zoning would clean up this discrepancy. He stated current plans include four building foot prints and his plans going forward also involve four foot prints. He added his proposal will provide for use of about 1/3 of the area of these lots for walking trails.

J. Hager shared base information for the parcels as attached. She noted when considering re-zoning what a petitioner might do is not important, what ANY person could do is what should be considered. In this case, with combined land and a new roadway 12 units could likely be established and perhaps 16 units, although wetland and river way buffers will restrict the use of much of the rear of the lots. She added unfortunately it is unlikely proposed river trails on the Town land south of these parcels could be continued to this land due to topography.

W. Talcott noted a triangle of Rural Residential zoning is left isolated. This would remain for the time being unless re-zoned in the future. This land is not really useable for anything regardless. Mr. Stevens stated his conceptual plan showed the wetlands/river and fire code restricted use to four duplexes.

W. Talcott added a re-zoning could also allow uses beyond currently allowed Rural Residential uses that apply now.

D. Mason asked how long the variance for frontage conditioned on only building a single family home is in effect for on 430 Putnam Hill Road. J. Hager stated, according to the Building Commissioner, the variance is in effect until Sept 2026. She clarified just because there is a variance in effect, anyone can propose another use if it is in compliance with the zoning bylaw.

R. Nunnemacher of 24 Singletary Avenue, also a member of the Board of Assessors and a Registered Professional Land Surveyor, objected to a re-zoning being proposed that refers only to the street address of the parcels. He noted how often these addresses can change and that if this moves forward, the Planning Board should amend the action to refer to deed book and pages.

Dennis LaForce of 27 Whitins Road objected to the proposed re-zoning. He noted he's lived in the Village for over 45 years and has been a water commissioner for decades. He said the Village zoning feels very intentional to him with a Village nucleus surrounded by Rural Residential zoning. He felt re-zoning to Village was a slippery slope promoting more re-zoning and wedging in more homes. He noted it isn't even certain that the Water District can supply water to these homes as several of their wells may not be on their property.

James Baker of 442 Putnam Hill Road said his family has been in Manchaug since 1927. He is third generation. He stated this land is most wet with a lot of ledge. He was against these changes.

Ian Hutchinson of 5 West Second Street expressed concerns with changing the character of the Village. He noted Mr. Stevens is trying to hold the Village water supply hostage to get a re-zoning when he should just donate the land to the District. He noted existing trails aren't maintained so there is no need for more and there is no parking. He said this isn't meant to clean up zoning lines, it's just meant to maximize Mr. Steven's profits.

The Chair noted the legal issues involved with the wells is not within the purview of the Board or their consideration of this re-zoning proposal.

Raouf Mankaryous, co-owner of 432 Putnam Hill Road had concerns about his abutting septic system and drainage, but he worried about the domino effect of re-zonings combined with the new ADU statute. He felt there should be a master plan for potential re-zoning with a limit on the number of units before re-zoning is considered.

The Chair took a straw-pole of those present for and against to gauge what further commentary might reveal.

By law the Board must provide a recommendation on every zoning article. It is not binding on voters; it is just a recommendation. Voters have the final say whether they support and article or do not support it. A vote to approve a zoning article must receive a 2/3rds vote of Town Meeting. Town Meeting is scheduled for September 21, 2026 at 7 PM this year. She also provided general guidance relative to the Board's consideration of proposed articles.

W. Talcott stressed this article will still go the Town Meeting so regardless of the Board's recommendation those interested should attend. The voting standard requiring 2/3rds of those present and voting to approve a zoning change is higher as it amounts to changing the rules during the game.

He stated this proposal is messy. He noted a potential benefit of adding more area for services allowed in the Village district, but this proposal is only for two lots.

D. Mason agreed and noted leaving an island of Rural Residential zoning isn't how zoning should be done. He noted re-zoning these entire lots would make the Village zoning deeper than the Village zoning to the east of Putnam Hill Road.

As requested, J. Hager explained what a yes and no vote on this article will do.

M. Gagan noted the inconsistency of what is proposed versus abutting land.

W. Stanhope added that re-zonings can be beneficial when carefully considered and placed in the right locations. This proposal is awkward and piecemeal.

Motion: To not recommend that Town Meeting approve this article, R. Largess Jr.
2nd: E. McCallum
Vote: E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Talcott – aye, W. Stanhope – aye

### Amendments to Accessory Apartment Bylaw

J. Hager made a brief presentation as attached. The Board and those in attendance discussed various aspects of the two versions. R. Nunnemacher asked who would police number of occupants if this provision is maintained. J. Hager re-stated a previous observation of D. Mason that no one will police this element unless there is an issue. Land owners would bear the cost of evictions if necessary. R. Nunnemacher felt this provision would be more trouble than its worth. Gary Primo of 93 Fairway View Drive asked if the one-bedroom restriction is removed what will otherwise limit the bedrooms? J. Hager stated that all units must still comply with Board of Health regulations for septic systems (Title V) and any regulations related to public health that may regulate occupancy. He didn't feel it was necessary for the landowner to live on the property. The majority of the Board felt the ADU needs to be clearly subordinate, but doesn't need to necessarily look like a barn or garage. There was extensive discussion on whether LADUs, non-protected use ADUS which are generally over 900 s.f., should also be limited to no larger than 50% of the principle dwelling. P. Nichols of 167 Burbank Road stated this in effect punishes those who have smaller primary dwellings who may actually have a greater need for additional space as opposed to those with large homes. A. Mattei of 21 Golf Ridge Drive said she was concerned about approving these changes now considering there may be another law that says you have to allowed duplexes on every lot that could otherwise have a single family home. She noted this will start the housing explosion and allow even more ADUS on a lot. J. Hager clarified this law does not exist to date, but current ADU law only allows one protected use ADU on a lot regardless of the type of home on a lot. She stated whether or not the proposed duplex law proceeds has little to do with whether this local bylaw should be cleaned up unless she is suggesting that Sutton should prohibit ADUs over 900 s.f. She felt the waiver provision should not be maintained.

The Board settled on the 7/27/26 version that mirrors state law with the proportional requirements in provisions d. and e. and losing the waiver provision.

Motion: To recommend that Town Meeting approve this article as revised, R. Largess Jr.
2nd: E. McCallum
Vote: E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Talcott – aye, W. Stanhope – aye

Motion: To close the public hearing, W. Talcott
2nd: E. McCallum
Vote: 5-0-0, E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Talcott – aye, W. Stanhope – aye

Motion: To adjourn, R. Largess Jr.
2nd: E. McCallum
Vote: E. McCallum- aye, R Largess Jr. – aye, M. Gagan – aye, W. Talcott – aye, W. Stanhope – aye

Adjourned 9:45 pm
